## 4. Boot / launch path files

### 4.1 `arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c` (full)
```c
/* RISC-V kernel boot stage */
#include <os/elf.h>
#include <pgtable.h>
#include <sbi.h>

typedef void (*kernel_entry_t)(unsigned long);

extern unsigned char _elf_main[];
extern unsigned _length_main;

/*
 * using 2MB large page
 * kva = kpa + 0xffff_ffc0_0000_0000 use 2MB page
 * map all physical memory
 */
void map_kernel_page(PTE *pgdir)
{
    clear_pgdir(pgdir);
    /*
     * first level:
     * 0xffff_ffc0_5000_0000: VPN2 = 0x101
     * 0x0000_0000_5000_0000: VPN2 = 0x001
     */
    set_pfn(pgdir + 0x101, (PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
    set_attribute(pgdir + 0x101, _PAGE_PRESENT);
    set_pfn(pgdir + 0x001, (PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
    set_attribute(pgdir + 0x001, _PAGE_PRESENT);
    /*
     * last level:
     * 0x5000_0000: VPN1 = 0x80
     * 256MB = 2MB * 128
     */
    PTE *last_level_pgdir = (PTE*)(PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE);
    clear_pgdir(last_level_pgdir);
    for(int i = 0; i < 128; i++){
        PTE* pgtable = last_level_pgdir + 0x80 + i;
        set_pfn(pgtable, (0x50000000 + LARGE_PAGE_SIZE * i ) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_PRESENT);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_READ);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_WRITE);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_EXEC);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_ACCESSED);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_DIRTY);
    }
}

void enable_vm()
{
    set_satp(SATP_MODE_SV39, 0, (PGDIR_PA >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT));
    local_flush_tlb_all();
}

/* Sv-39 mode
 * 0x0000_0000_0000_0000-0x0000_003f_ffff_ffff is for user mode
 * 0xffff_ffc0_0000_0000-0xffff_ffff_ffff_ffff is for kernel mode
 */
void setup_vm()
{
    // map kernel virtual address(kva) to kernel physical
    map_kernel_page((PTE *)PGDIR_PA);
    // enable virtual memory
    enable_vm();
}

uintptr_t directmap(uintptr_t kva, uintptr_t pgdir)
{
    return kva;
}

kernel_entry_t start_kernel = NULL;

/* start here */
int boot_kernel(unsigned long mhartid)
{
    if(mhartid == 0) {
        // setup memory mapping
        setup_vm();
        sbi_console_putstr("> [INIT] Set Up Kernel Page Table Successfully.\n\r");
        // load kernel
        start_kernel = (kernel_entry_t)load_elf(_elf_main, _length_main, PGDIR_PA, directmap);
        sbi_console_putstr("> [INIT] Copy Kernel to Memory Successfully.\n\r");
    }else {
        enable_vm();
    }
    start_kernel(mhartid);
    return 0;
}
```
**Note the root PTE at `[0x101]` is a pointer PTE with only `_PAGE_PRESENT` set** — that's the exact PTE value you copy into every process pgdir: `new_pgdir_kva[0x101] = boot_pgdir_kva[0x101];`. Also note the kernel's leaf mappings do **not** set `_PAGE_USER`, so user code cannot touch kernel memory (hence `enable_sum()` when the kernel touches user buffers).

### 4.2 `arch/riscv/kernel/start.S` (full)
```asm
.section ".entry_function","ax"
ENTRY(_start)
  /* Mask all interrupts */
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero
  csrw CSR_SIP, zero

  /* Disable FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space */
  li t0, SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* Load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  csrr t0, CSR_MHARTID
  bnez t0, secondary

  /* Clear BSS for flat non-ELF images */
  la a3, __bss_start
  la a4, __BSS_END__
  ble a4, a3, clear_bss_done
clear_bss:
  sd zero, (a3)
  add a3, a3, RISCV_SZPTR
  blt a3, a4, clear_bss
clear_bss_done:

  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core0_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_0
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call main

secondary:
  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core1_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_1
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call smp_init
END(_start)
```
`tp` starts as `&kernel_pcb[cpu]` and `sscratch = 0` marks "in kernel" (see `exception_handler_entry`: `csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp; bnez tp, from_user`). For user tasks, `init_pcb_stack` sets `pt_regs->sscratch = (reg_t)pcb`, so on the first `sret` the PCB pointer moves into `sscratch` and user `tp` is whatever the ELF sets.

### 4.4 `init/main.c` — the pieces that constrain you
```c
static void init_pcb_stack(ptr_t kernel_stack, ptr_t user_stack, ptr_t entry_point, pcb_t *pcb)
{
    regs_context_t *pt_regs = (regs_context_t *)(kernel_stack - sizeof(regs_context_t));
    pcb->kernel_sp -= sizeof(regs_context_t);

    /* initialization registers: ra, sp, gp, sepc, sstatus, sepc, sscratch */
    pt_regs->regs[1] = (reg_t)entry_point;      //ra
    pt_regs->regs[2] = (reg_t)user_stack;       //sp
    pt_regs->regs[3] = (reg_t)__global_pointer$;//gp
    pt_regs->sstatus = (reg_t)SR_SPIE;          //SPP = 0, SPIE = 1
    pt_regs->sepc = (reg_t)entry_point;         //sepc
    pt_regs->sscratch = (reg_t)pcb;             //sscratch = tp
}
```
This is `static` in `main.c` — **you must replicate it inside `sched.c` for `do_exec`** (and `extern void __global_pointer$();` is already declared at the top of `sched.c` for exactly that reason). Note `kernel_stack` here is the *top* kva and `pcb->kernel_sp` must already equal that top before the call, since it subtracts in place.

## 5. SD card helpers and the swap area

`arch/riscv/include/sbi.h`:
```c
static inline uintptr_t sbi_sd_write(
    unsigned int mem_address, unsigned int num_of_blocks,
    unsigned int block_id)
{
    return SBI_CALL_3(
        SBI_SD_WRITE, mem_address, num_of_blocks, block_id);
}

static inline uintptr_t sbi_sd_read(
    unsigned int mem_address, unsigned int num_of_blocks,
    unsigned int block_id)
{
    return SBI_CALL_3(
        SBI_SD_READ, mem_address, num_of_blocks, block_id);
}
```
with `#define SBI_SD_WRITE 10` / `#define SBI_SD_READ 11` in `arch/riscv/include/asm/sbidef.h`.

`mem_address` is `unsigned int` ⇒ **32-bit physical address** — pass the raw `pa` (`0x51000000..0x5e000000` fits), never a kva. Confirmed by the bootloader (`arch/riscv/boot/bootblock.S`, reading into `0x50201000` with `a1 = 64` blocks, `a2 = block_id`) and by Project 6's driver, which always wraps with `kva2pa`:
```c
    sbi_sd_read(kva2pa(SUPERBLOCK_CACHE), 1, SUPERBLOCK_ID);
    sbi_sd_write(kva2pa(BLOCKMAP_CACHE), 64, BLOCKMAP_BEGIN_ID);
```

**Swap layout** (`include/os/mm.h`): `#define SWAP_BEGIN 2048`, `#define DISK_PAGE_NUM 256`, `disk_page_t{ uint8_t valid; } disk_page[DISK_PAGE_NUM];`

Block size is 512 B ⇒ 8 blocks per 4 KB page. The canonical mapping is:
```
disk slot i  ->  block_id = SWAP_BEGIN + i * 8,  num_of_blocks = 8
```
covering blocks 2048…4095 (1 MB of swap = 256 pages). The Makefile creates that region:
```make
image: bootblock kernelimage createimage
	./createimage --extended bootblock kernelimage
	dd if=/dev/zero of=image oflag=append conv=notrunc bs=512 count=4096
```
i.e. 4096 zero-filled sectors (2 MB) appended after the kernel image.

For the swapped-out PTE encoding, the natural scheme given the helpers: on eviction, `clear_attribute(pte, _PAGE_PRESENT)`, `set_attribute(pte, _PAGE_SOFT)`, `set_pfn(pte, disk_slot_index)` — `set_pfn` masks with `ATTRIBUTE_MASK` (bits 8:0) so `_PAGE_SOFT` and the R/W/X/U bits survive. On fault, `if (pte != 0 && !(pte & _PAGE_PRESENT) && (pte & _PAGE_SOFT))` → `sbi_sd_read(new_pa, 8, SWAP_BEGIN + get_pfn(pte)*8)`, free the disk slot, `set_pfn(pte, new_pa >> 12)`, `clear_attribute(pte, _PAGE_SOFT)`, `set_attribute(pte, _PAGE_PRESENT|_PAGE_ACCESSED|_PAGE_DIRTY)`, then `local_flush_tlb_all()`.

`user_page[i].pgtable` (`PTE*`) exists precisely so `selete_page()`/`write_to_sd()` can reach the single PTE that maps the victim frame: NRU = scan `user_page[]` for `valid && !pin && pgtable != NULL && !get_attribute(*pgtable, _PAGE_ACCESSED)`, clearing `_PAGE_ACCESSED` as you sweep (second-chance) so a second pass always finds a victim. `pin=1` entries (kernel stacks, shm pages) and `pgtable == NULL` entries must be skipped.

The swap test is `test/swap.c`, which touches 32 pages at a wild address:
```c
#define LENGTH (4096 * 8)
int main()
{
    int flag = 1;
    unsigned long *array = (unsigned long *)0x20000000;
    for(int i = 0; i < LENGTH; i++){ *(array + i) = i; }
    for(int i = 0; i < LENGTH; i++){ if(*(array + i) != i){ flag = 0; } }
    ...

**How `current_running[cpu_id]` works:**
- `cpu_id` is a single **global `int` defined in `kernel/irq/irq.c`**, refreshed at the top of every trap: `cpu_id = get_current_cpu_id();`. It is safe to read only because `exception_handler_entry` takes the big `kernel_lock` (`call lock_kernel`) before calling `interrupt_helper`, and `ret_from_exception` releases it after reading `current_cpu_running`. - `interrupt_helper` also sets `current_cpu_running = current_running[cpu_id];` on entry; `ret_from_exception` re-reads it (`ld tp, current_cpu_running`) on exit. Therefore **`scheduler()` must update both** `current_running[cpu_id]` and `current_cpu_running`.
- Idle tasks are `kernel_pcb[0]` (hart 0, mask 1) and `kernel_pcb[1]` (hart 1, mask 2); they never enter `ready_queue`.
- `pcb_t.mask` is the affinity bitmask (`1`=core0, `2`=core1, `3`=both — documented in `README.txt`), set by `do_taskset`; `pcb_t.cpu_id` is the core the task is currently on, printed by `ps`.
- Every other subsystem writes through `current_running[cpu_id]` (`screen.c` cursor tracking, `time.c` timer, `binsem.c` binsem bookkeeping, `futex.c`, `mailbox.c`), so `scheduler()` must keep the pointer valid at all times — never leave it NULL.

Preemption helpers (`entry.S`) act on `tp`, not on `current_running`, which is the "trick" the comment above `scheduler()` refers to: `tp` only changes at `ret_from_exception`, so a `disable_preempt()`/`enable_preempt()` pair straddling a `scheduler()` call still decrements the same PCB's counter.

## 0. Key architectural facts you must honor (derived, read this first)

1. **There is no `switch_to` / context-switch assembly.** `scheduler()` only rewrites `current_running[cpu_id]`, `current_cpu_running`, and `satp`. The actual switch happens in `arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:ret_from_exception`, which does `ld tp, current_cpu_running` then `RESTORE_CONTEXT` (which loads `sp` from `PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)`). **If `scheduler()` does not write `current_cpu_running`, nothing switches.**
2. Consequence: a task that blocks inside a syscall **abandons its kernel stack frame** and, when later unblocked, resumes in *user mode* at `sepc`. The repo author documents this in `/workspace/README.md` item 7: *"进程只能阻塞在用户态…这一feature造成waitpid系统调用实现困难…本人的waitpid系统调用实现非常tricky。"* This is why `do_waitpid` receives `regs_context_t *regs`: `handle_syscall` already did `regs->sepc += 4`, so `regs->sepc -= 4` makes the blocked caller **re-execute the `ecall`** when it is rescheduled (retry loop).
3. `pcb_t.pgdir` is a **physical address** (`init/main.c`: `kernel_pcb[0].pgdir = (PTE*)PGDIR_PA;`). All page-table walks in kernel code must go through `pa2kva()`.
4. The kernel is mapped at `kva = pa + 0xffffffc000000000` by 2MB large pages covering `0x50000000..0x60000000`, installed under **root-PTE index `0x101`** (VPN2 of `0xffffffc050000000` = 0x101). Every new process pgdir must copy that one entry to keep the kernel addressable. Core 1 deletes the identity map (`smp.c`: `*(pgdir + 0x001) = 0;`), so a process pgdir must **not** contain entry `0x001`.
5. `sbi_sd_read/write` take a **32-bit physical address**, a block count, and a block id; blocks are 512 B ⇒ one 4 KB page = **8 blocks**. Swap area starts at block `SWAP_BEGIN` = 2048.

    last_level_pgdir = (PTE*)pa2kva((uintptr_t)last_level_pgdir);
    uintptr_t pa = get_pa((uintptr_t)*((PTE*)last_level_pgdir + VPN0)) | (va & PAGE_OFFSET_MASK);
    return pa2kva(pa);
}

```

**Critical:** `get_kva_of` is a pure *walker* — it never allocates. `init/main.c` passes it to `load_elf` as the `prepare_page_for_va` callback, so **`init_page_table()` must have already fully mapped the whole code region** before `load_elf` runs. Note also `set_pfn` preserves bits [8:0] (including `_PAGE_SOFT`), which makes `_PAGE_SOFT` usable as a "swapped out" marker.

### `max_priority_node` — called only by your `scheduler()`
The **complete reference implementation exists** in the repo at `/workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2/kernel/sched/sched.c` (part of the pristine round-0 tree, not stubbed). Verbatim:

```c
/*
 * Pick the ready task with the highest effective priority.  The effective
 * priority is the static priority plus an ageing bonus of one point for every
 * scheduling tick the task has already spent waiting, so that a low priority
 * task cannot starve forever.  Ties are won by the task that entered the
 * ready queue first, which keeps tasks of equal priority round-robin.
 */
list_node_t* max_priority_node(void)
{
    list_node_t *node;
    list_node_t *max_node = NULL;
    uint64_t max_priority = 0;
    uint64_t current_tick = get_ticks();

    for (node = ready_queue.next; node != &ready_queue; node = node->next) {
        pcb_t *task = list_entry(node, pcb_t, list);
        uint64_t waited_tick = 0;
        uint64_t priority;

        if (current_tick > task->ready_tick) {
            waited_tick = current_tick - task->ready_tick;
        }
        priority = (uint64_t)task->priority;
        if (timer_interval != 0) {
            priority += waited_tick / timer_interval;
        }

        if (max_node == NULL || priority > max_priority) {
            max_node = node;
            max_priority = priority;
        }
    }

    return max_node;
}
```
and the matching single-core `scheduler()` from the same file:
```c
void scheduler(void)
{
    pcb_t *prev = current_running;
    pcb_t *next;
    list_node_t *next_node;

    /* A task that is still runnable goes back to the tail of the ready queue.
     * pid0 is the idle task and never lives in the ready queue, and a task
     * that has just blocked itself is already parked somewhere else. */
    if (prev != &pid0_pcb && prev->status == TASK_RUNNING) {
        prev->status = TASK_READY;
        prev->ready_tick = get_ticks();
        list_add_tail(&prev->list, &ready_queue);
    }

    next_node = max_priority_node();
    if (next_node == NULL) {
        /* nothing is runnable, fall back to the idle task */
        next = &pid0_pcb;
    } else {
        list_del(next_node);
        next = list_entry(next_node, pcb_t, list);
    }

    next->status = TASK_RUNNING;
    current_running = next;

    /* every task owns its own cursor position */
    screen_cursor_x = current_running->cursor_x;
    screen_cursor_y = current_running->cursor_y;
}
```
For P4 you must additionally: index by `cpu_id`; skip ready tasks whose `mask` excludes this hart (`task->mask & (1 << cpu_id)`); fall back to `&kernel_pcb[cpu_id]`; set `next->cpu_id = cpu_id`; write `current_cpu_running = next;`; restore `screen_cursor_x[cpu_id]/screen_cursor_y[cpu_id]`; and switch `satp`.

### `set_satp` / `local_flush_tlb_all` — only existing call site, `arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c:47-51`
```c
void enable_vm()
{
    set_satp(SATP_MODE_SV39, 0, (PGDIR_PA >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT));
    local_flush_tlb_all();
}
```
⇒ in `scheduler()`: `set_satp(SATP_MODE_SV39, next->pid, ((uintptr_t)next->pgdir) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT); local_flush_tlb_all();` (asid can be 0 if you always flush; `set_satp` already issues an `sfence.vma` before the `csrw`, so an extra flush after is the safe idiom).

### `alloc_page_helper` / `share_pgtable` — **do not exist in Project 4**
`alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir)` only appears in Project5/Project6 (`extern uintptr_t alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir);` in their `mm.h`, stubbed in their `mm.c` with the comment `// pgdir is pa. if va is not mapped, then mapped it`). `share_pgtable` appears nowhere in the workspace. In P4 the equivalent "walk-and-allocate" logic must be a static helper you write inside `mm.c` (used by `init_page_table`, `handle_page_fault`, `shm_page_get`, and `do_exec`). `alloc_page` (P3's `allocPage`) also does not exist in P4.

## 4. Boot / launch path files

### 4.1 `arch/riscv/kernel/boot.c` (full)
```c
/* RISC-V kernel boot stage */
#include <os/elf.h>
#include <pgtable.h>
#include <sbi.h>

typedef void (*kernel_entry_t)(unsigned long);

extern unsigned char _elf_main[];
extern unsigned _length_main;

/*
 * using 2MB large page
 * kva = kpa + 0xffff_ffc0_0000_0000 use 2MB page
 * map all physical memory
 */
void map_kernel_page(PTE *pgdir)
{
    clear_pgdir(pgdir);
    /*
     * first level:
     * 0xffff_ffc0_5000_0000: VPN2 = 0x101
     * 0x0000_0000_5000_0000: VPN2 = 0x001
     */
    set_pfn(pgdir + 0x101, (PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
    set_attribute(pgdir + 0x101, _PAGE_PRESENT);
    set_pfn(pgdir + 0x001, (PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
    set_attribute(pgdir + 0x001, _PAGE_PRESENT);
    /*
     * last level:
     * 0x5000_0000: VPN1 = 0x80
     * 256MB = 2MB * 128
     */
    PTE *last_level_pgdir = (PTE*)(PGDIR_PA + NORMAL_PAGE_SIZE);
    clear_pgdir(last_level_pgdir);
    for(int i = 0; i < 128; i++){
        PTE* pgtable = last_level_pgdir + 0x80 + i;
        set_pfn(pgtable, (0x50000000 + LARGE_PAGE_SIZE * i ) >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_PRESENT);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_READ);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_WRITE);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_EXEC);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_ACCESSED);
        set_attribute(pgtable, _PAGE_DIRTY);
    }
}

void enable_vm()
{
    set_satp(SATP_MODE_SV39, 0, (PGDIR_PA >> NORMAL_PAGE_SHIFT));
    local_flush_tlb_all();
}

/* Sv-39 mode
 * 0x0000_0000_0000_0000-0x0000_003f_ffff_ffff is for user mode
 * 0xffff_ffc0_0000_0000-0xffff_ffff_ffff_ffff is for kernel mode
 */
void setup_vm()
{
    // map kernel virtual address(kva) to kernel physical
    map_kernel_page((PTE *)PGDIR_PA);
    // enable virtual memory
    enable_vm();
}

uintptr_t directmap(uintptr_t kva, uintptr_t pgdir)
{
    return kva;
}

kernel_entry_t start_kernel = NULL;

/* start here */
int boot_kernel(unsigned long mhartid)
{
    if(mhartid == 0) {
        // setup memory mapping
        setup_vm();
        sbi_console_putstr("> [INIT] Set Up Kernel Page Table Successfully.\n\r");
        // load kernel
        start_kernel = (kernel_entry_t)load_elf(_elf_main, _length_main, PGDIR_PA, directmap);
        sbi_console_putstr("> [INIT] Copy Kernel to Memory Successfully.\n\r");
    }else {
        enable_vm();
    }
    start_kernel(mhartid);
    return 0;
}
```
**Note the root PTE at `[0x101]` is a pointer PTE with only `_PAGE_PRESENT` set** — that's the exact PTE value you copy into every process pgdir: `new_pgdir_kva[0x101] = boot_pgdir_kva[0x101];`. Also note the kernel's leaf mappings do **not** set `_PAGE_USER`, so user code cannot touch kernel memory (hence `enable_sum()` when the kernel touches user buffers).

### 4.2 `arch/riscv/kernel/start.S` (full)
```asm
.section ".entry_function","ax"
ENTRY(_start)
  /* Mask all interrupts */
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero
  csrw CSR_SIP, zero

  /* Disable FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space */
  li t0, SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* Load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  csrr t0, CSR_MHARTID
  bnez t0, secondary

  /* Clear BSS for flat non-ELF images */
  la a3, __bss_start
  la a4, __BSS_END__
  ble a4, a3, clear_bss_done
clear_bss:
  sd zero, (a3)
  add a3, a3, RISCV_SZPTR
  blt a3, a4, clear_bss
clear_bss_done:

  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core0_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_0
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call main

secondary:
  /* setup C environment */
  ld tp, core1_tp
  ld sp, kernel_stack_1
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, zero

  la a0, riscv_dtb
  sd a1, (a0)

  call smp_init
END(_start)
```
`tp` starts as `&kernel_pcb[cpu]` and `sscratch = 0` marks "in kernel" (see `exception_handler_entry`: `csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp; bnez tp, from_user`). For user tasks, `init_pcb_stack` sets `pt_regs->sscratch = (reg_t)pcb`, so on the first `sret` the PCB pointer moves into `sscratch` and user `tp` is whatever the ELF sets.

    la a3, __bss_start

### 4.4 `init/main.c` — the pieces that constrain you
```c
static void init_pcb_stack(ptr_t kernel_stack, ptr_t user_stack, ptr_t entry_point, pcb_t *pcb)
{
    regs_context_t *pt_regs = (regs_context_t *)(kernel_stack - sizeof(regs_context_t));
    pcb->kernel_sp -= sizeof(regs_context_t);

    /* initialization registers: ra, sp, gp, sepc, sstatus, sepc, sscratch */
    pt_regs->regs[1] = (reg_t)entry_point;      //ra
    pt_regs->regs[2] = (reg_t)user_stack;       //sp
    pt_regs->regs[3] = (reg_t)__global_pointer$;//gp
    pt_regs->sstatus = (reg_t)SR_SPIE;          //SPP = 0, SPIE = 1
    pt_regs->sepc = (reg_t)entry_point;         //sepc
    pt_regs->sscratch = (reg_t)pcb;             //sscratch = tp
}
```
This is `static` in `main.c` — **you must replicate it inside `sched.c` for `do_exec`** (and `extern void __global_pointer$();` is already declared at the top of `sched.c` for exactly that reason). Note `kernel_stack` here is the *top* kva and `pcb->kernel_sp` must already equal that top before the call, since it subtracts in place.

## 5. SD card helpers and the swap area

`arch/riscv/include/sbi.h`:
```c
static inline uintptr_t sbi_sd_write(
    unsigned int mem_address, unsigned int num_of_blocks,
    unsigned int block_id)
{
    return SBI_CALL_3(
        SBI_SD_WRITE, mem_address, num_of_blocks, block_id);
}

static inline uintptr_t sbi_sd_read(
    unsigned int mem_address, unsigned int num_of_blocks,
    unsigned int block_id)
{
    return SBI_CALL_3(
        SBI_SD_READ, mem_address, num_of_blocks, block_id);
}
```
with `#define SBI_SD_WRITE 10` / `#define SBI_SD_READ 11` in `arch/riscv/include/asm/sbidef.h`.

`mem_address` is `unsigned int` ⇒ **32-bit physical address** — pass the raw `pa` (`0x51000000..0x5e000000` fits), never a kva. Confirmed by the bootloader (`arch/riscv/boot/bootblock.S`, reading into `0x50201000` with `a1 = 64` blocks, `a2 = block_id`) and by Project 6's driver, which always wraps with `kva2pa`:
```c
    sbi_sd_read(kva2pa(SUPERBLOCK_CACHE), 1, SUPERBLOCK_ID);
    sbi_sd_write(kva2pa(BLOCKMAP_CACHE), 64, BLOCKMAP_BEGIN_ID);
```

**Swap layout** (`include/os/mm.h`): `#define SWAP_BEGIN 2048`, `#define DISK_PAGE_NUM 256`, `disk_page_t{ uint8_t valid; } disk_page[DISK_PAGE_NUM];`

Block size is 512 B ⇒ 8 blocks per 4 KB page. The canonical mapping is:
```
disk slot i  ->  block_id = SWAP_BEGIN + i * 8,  num_of_blocks = 8
```
covering blocks 2048…4095 (1 MB of swap = 256 pages). The Makefile creates that region:
```make
image: bootblock kernelimage createimage
	./createimage --extended bootblock kernelimage
	dd if=/dev/zero of=image oflag=append conv=notrunc bs=512 count=4096
```
i.e. 4096 zero-filled sectors (2 MB) appended after the kernel image.

For the swapped-out PTE encoding, the natural scheme given the helpers: on eviction, `clear_attribute(pte, _PAGE_PRESENT)`, `set_attribute(pte, _PAGE_SOFT)`, `set_pfn(pte, disk_slot_index)` — `set_pfn` masks with `ATTRIBUTE_MASK` (bits 8:0) so `_PAGE_SOFT` and the R/W/X/U bits survive. On fault, `if (pte != 0 && !(pte & _PAGE_PRESENT) && (pte & _PAGE_SOFT))` → `sbi_sd_read(new_pa, 8, SWAP_BEGIN + get_pfn(pte)*8)`, free the disk slot, `set_pfn(pte, new_pa >> 12)`, `clear_attribute(pte, _PAGE_SOFT)`, `set_attribute(pte, _PAGE_PRESENT|_PAGE_ACCESSED|_PAGE_DIRTY)`, then `local_flush_tlb_all()`.

`user_page[i].pgtable` (`PTE*`) exists precisely so `selete_page()`/`write_to_sd()` can reach the single PTE that maps the victim frame: NRU = scan `user_page[]` for `valid && !pin && pgtable != NULL && !get_attribute(*pgtable, _PAGE_ACCESSED)`, clearing `_PAGE_ACCESSED` as you sweep (second-chance) so a second pass always finds a victim. `pin=1` entries (kernel stacks, shm pages) and `pgtable == NULL` entries must be skipped.

The swap test is `test/swap.c`, which touches 32 pages at a wild address:
```c
#define LENGTH (4096 * 8)
int main()
{
    int flag = 1;
    unsigned long *array = (unsigned long *)0x20000000;
    for(int i = 0; i < LENGTH; i++){ *(array + i) = i; }
    for(int i = 0; i < LENGTH; i++){ if(*(array + i) != i){ flag = 0; } }
    ...
}
```
(`LENGTH` counts `unsigned long`s ⇒ 256 KB ⇒ 64 pages at `0x20000000`, all demand-allocated.) `test/rw.c` writes to arbitrary addresses passed as decimal argv strings, so `handle_page_fault` must map *any* user VA on demand.

int smp_init_flag = 0;

void smp_init()
{
    PTE *pgdir = (PTE*)PGDIR_PA;
    *(pgdir + 0x001) = 0;
    smp_init_flag = 1;

    enable_interrupt();
    setup_exception();
    sbi_set_timer(get_ticks() + timer_interval);
    while (1){
        __asm__ __volatile__("wfi\n\r":::);
    }
}

void lock_kernel()   { spin_lock_acquire(&kernel_lock); }
void unlock_kernel() { spin_lock_release(&kernel_lock); }
```
`get_current_cpu_id` is `arch/riscv/kernel/smp.S`: `csrr a0, CSR_MHARTID; jr ra`.

**How `current_running[cpu_id]` works:**
- `cpu_id` is a single **global `int` defined in `kernel/irq/irq.c`**, refreshed at the top of every trap: `cpu_id = get_current_cpu_id();`. It is safe to read only because `exception_handler_entry` takes the big `kernel_lock` (`call lock_kernel`) before calling `interrupt_helper`, and `ret_from_exception` releases it after reading `current_cpu_running`. So all kernel-side code (including your `scheduler()`) runs mutually excluded and can rely on `cpu_id`.
- `interrupt_helper` also sets `current_cpu_running = current_running[cpu_id];` on entry; `ret_from_exception` re-reads it (`ld tp, current_cpu_running`) on exit. Therefore **`scheduler()` must update both** `current_running[cpu_id]` and `current_cpu_running`.
- Idle tasks are `kernel_pcb[0]` (hart 0, mask 1) and `kernel_pcb[1]` (hart 1, mask 2); they never enter `ready_queue`.
- `pcb_t.mask` is the affinity bitmask (`1`=core0, `2`=core1, `3`=both — documented in `README.txt`), set by `do_taskset`; `pcb_t.cpu_id` is the core the task is currently on, printed by `ps`.
- Every other subsystem writes through `current_running[cpu_id]` (`screen.c` cursor tracking, `time.c` timer, `binsem.c` binsem bookkeeping, `futex.c`, `mailbox.c`), so `scheduler()` must keep the pointer valid at all times — never leave it NULL.

Preemption helpers (`entry.S`) act on `tp`, not on `current_running`, which is the "trick" the comment above `scheduler()` refers to: `tp` only changes at `ret_from_exception`, so a `disable_preempt()`/`enable_preempt()` pair straddling a `scheduler()` call still decrements the same PCB's counter.

  unsigned char* file_content;
  int* file_length;
} ElfFile;

#define ELF_FILE_NUM <n>

```c
int get_elf_file(const char *file_name, unsigned char **binary, int *length)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    if (strcmp(elf_files[i].file_name,file_name) == 0) {
      *binary = elf_files[i].file_content;
      *length = *elf_files[i].file_length;

}
```

#!/bin/bash
# Host-side functional tests for the kernel subsystems implemented in this repo.
#
# Kernel code is compiled natively (with small shims under hostshim/ standing in
# for the RISC-V specific headers) and driven directly, so the scheduling,
# synchronisation, IPC and file-system logic can be executed and asserted on
# without a board or an emulator.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
SHIM="$ROOT/agent_tests/hostshim"
OUT=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0

run_case() {
    local name=$1; shift
    if ! gcc -g -O0 -o "$OUT/$name" "$@" 2>"$OUT/$name.log"; then
        echo "[$name] COMPILE FAILED"
        sed -n '1,40p' "$OUT/$name.log"
        fail=1
        return
    fi
    if ! timeout 60 "$OUT/$name"; then
        echo "[$name] RUN FAILED"
        fail=1
    fi
}

P2A="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1"
run_case p2a_sched \
    "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2a_sched_test.c" \
    "$P2A/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2A/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
    -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2A/include" -I"$P2A/drivers" -I"$P2A/arch/riscv/include"

# get_ticks() reads the RISC-V `time` CSR, which the host cannot execute.  Swap
# just that one read for a counter the test drives; timer_check() -- the code
# actually under test -- is compiled verbatim.
host_time_c() {
    python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
asm = '''    __asm__ __volatile__(
        "rdtime %0"
        : "=r"(time_elapsed));'''
assert asm in src, "get_ticks() no longer looks the way the test expects"
src = src.replace(asm, "    time_elapsed = host_get_ticks();")
src = "extern unsigned long host_get_ticks(void);\n" + src
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(src)
PY
}

P2B="$ROOT/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" ]; then
    host_time_c "$P2B/kernel/sched/time.c" "$OUT/p2b_time.c"
    run_case p2b_sched \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p2b_sched_test.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/lock.c" \
        "$P2B/kernel/locking/futex.c" "$P2B/kernel/locking/binsem.c" \
        "$OUT/p2b_time.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P2B/include" -I"$P2B/drivers" -I"$P2B/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P3="$ROOT/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" ]; then
    run_case p3_proc \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p3_proc_test.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/sched/sched.c" "$P3/kernel/syscall/mailbox.c" \
        "$P3/kernel/locking/binsem.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P3/include" -I"$P3/drivers" -I"$P3/arch/riscv/include"
fi

P6="$ROOT/Project6-File_System"
if [ -f "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" ]; then
    run_case p6_fs \
        "$ROOT/agent_tests/p6_fs_test.c" \
        "$P6/kernel/fs/fs.c" "$P6/kernel/fs/file.c" \
        -I"$SHIM" -I"$P6/include" -I"$P6/drivers" -I"$P6/arch/riscv/include"
fi

rm -rf "$OUT"
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "SOME TESTS FAILED"
    exit 1
fi
echo "ALL HOST TESTS PASSED"
